title: Focused dynamic lens routing with fingerprinted selective reuse
summary: Add one dependency-neutral deterministic routing policy over the incumbent 26-lens signal engine; adapt Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate to stage-specific focused routes; preserve complete dispositions, fail-closed overflow through a protected content-addressed provider, per-lens evidence reuse, and zero lens workers in Build, Fix, and EM.

current_state.summary: The incumbent signal engine scores all 26 lenses as deep/light/n/a with an eight-deep cap and security/architecture floors. Product and Plan still use legacy strategy routing, Design forces only solution-design, automatic Review/Evaluate projects four or five sweep lenses, retry membership follows prior failures rather than canonical per-lens input changes, and the sealed zero-lens delivery mode currently suppresses Evaluate and EM together with Build/Fix. Canonical finding 6ea9aff0107f4bb6 additionally proves that worktree-side expanded-route issuance, clock, RSA verification, and consumption are not protected from worker monkeypatching. Existing ReviewKernel evidence, leases, native dispatch, storage, and telemetry are retained, while authority moves outside the worker checkout and interpreter.

alternatives.name: Shared pure policy with incumbent adapters
alternatives.description: Introduce one standard-library-only pure routing-policy module and keep current signal scoring, stage lifecycle, ReviewKernel provenance, signing, storage, and telemetry as consuming adapters.

gains: One deterministic disposition, cap, overflow, and fingerprint contract serves every routed stage
Reuses mature graph floors, scoped evidence views, leases, atomic collection, and native lifecycle enforcement
Keeps stage-specific evidence ownership explicit without copying an earlier route forward
costs: Requires a versioned compatibility reader for prior deep/light/n/a route history
Touches several stage adapters and gates even though the policy core is one module
Requires conservative per-lens relevance declarations before evidence may be reused
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A second independent router consumer needs non-Python execution or stage adapters cannot express their context without importing ReviewKernel internals.

alternatives.name: Independent policy in each stage
alternatives.description: Patch Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate separately, keeping selection and evidence rules next to each stage gate.

gains: Small initial change in each individual stage
costs: Duplicates canonicalization, disposition validation, cap behavior, privacy, and fingerprint logic
Makes equal-input determinism across stages difficult to prove
Allows mandatory-risk and covered-by semantics to drift between gates
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The requirement is narrowed to one routed stage and cross-stage determinism is explicitly removed.

alternatives.name: Replace the signal engine and ReviewKernel
alternatives.description: Create a new router, evidence store, dispatcher, retry engine, and result collector around the new disposition vocabulary.

gains: No legacy route vocabulary inside the new implementation
A single greenfield data model from context through collection
costs: Discards incumbent graph floors, scoped views, host-observed leases, collection atomicity, and provenance
Creates a broad migration and regression surface unrelated to the requirement
Delays focused routing behind a full review-system replacement
tradeoffs.revisit_when: ReviewKernel provenance or storage is separately approved for replacement and a migration plan preserves every canonical evidence receipt.

authority_alternatives.name: New packaged content-addressed control-plane provider
authority_alternatives.description: Package taskplane/expanded_route_authority_provider.py as an immutable content-addressed object and have the orchestrator execute it in a separate trusted process from an external protected locator and 0600 authority store.
gains: Removes issuance, real time, exact RSA verification, and one-use consumption from both the worker checkout and interpreter
Reuses the proven durably-protected-issuer custody and atomic-recovery pattern without sharing terminal-finalization authority
Keeps normal routes and rollback independent from the exceptional-route provider
costs: Adds one packaged provider module, content manifest, external locator, custody store, and recovery path
Requires orchestrator installation and permission checks before expanded routes can execute
authority_alternatives.revisit_when: A general authenticated host control-plane service already exists and can preserve this exact source, custody, binding, and atomic-consume contract with a smaller operational surface.

authority_alternatives.name: Extend the existing terminal authority provider
authority_alternatives.description: Add expanded-route approval and consumption to taskplane/terminal_truth.py and its durably-protected issuer.
gains: Reuses existing root-private custody, lock, immutable write, recovery, and receipt patterns directly
Adds no second protected provider lifecycle
costs: Couples independent route approval and terminal-finalization subjects, keys, recovery, revocation, and blast radius
Makes route-provider rollback capable of disturbing terminal truth
authority_alternatives.revisit_when: Terminal and expanded-route authorities acquire one approved subject, key lifecycle, revocation policy, and failure domain.

authority_alternatives.name: Separate host service
authority_alternatives.description: Move expanded-route authority to an authenticated local daemon or remote host service.
gains: Potential reuse by multiple repositories and runtimes
costs: Adds service authentication, availability, deployment, upgrade, and recovery surfaces
Introduces a network or daemon dependency for a narrow local exceptional action
authority_alternatives.revisit_when: Multiple independent control-plane actions require a shared continuously available host authority.

decision: Select the shared pure policy because the approved behavior is one cross-stage invariant while context and execution remain stage-owned. For canonical finding 6ea9aff0107f4bb6, select the new packaged content-addressed control-plane provider: it is the smallest authority boundary that follows the graph's selected durably-protected-issuer custody precedent while removing authority from the worker checkout and interpreter without coupling it to terminal finalization or adding a host service. Incumbent adapters retain proven scoring, dispatch, and evidence collection; taskplane_lite becomes request-only.

contracts.description: One policy version deterministically converts a validated stage context and 26 scored catalog rows into the smallest sufficient ordered focused route.
Every Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate route has exactly one evidenced execute_deep, execute_light, covered_by, or not_applicable disposition for each of the 26 catalog lenses.
Only Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate may execute selected lenses; Build, Fix, and EM prove zero lens-worker starts across every terminal lifecycle outcome.

A separately executed protected provider may issue and atomically consume one exact Plan/Evaluate route above four lenses after validating immutable provider source, external custody, real time, and an exact RSA approval receipt; the worktree adapter is request-only.

An external orchestrator-owned 0700 provider root holds a 0600 content-addressed locator, issuer key, approver-key manifest, receipt journal, and atomic one-use consumption state, with no symlink, relocation, worktree, or environment fallback.
Immutable route and per-lens canonical input fingerprints bind selection, evidence reuse, invalidation, policy version, and catalog version.
Bounded redacted records expose stage, selected count and reasons, estimated/actual tokens, runtime, cache reuse, invalidation, terminal status, and route fingerprint.

expanded_route_authority.execution_owner: orchestrator control plane in a separate trusted Python process
expanded_route_authority.worker_adapter: taskplane/taskplane_lite.py serializes a closed request and consumes a provider-sealed decision; it cannot choose the provider, supply time or verification functions, mint authority, inspect custody, or declare consumption

external_locator.location: orchestrator-configured absolute path outside the worker-controlled checkout
external_locator.validation: Open without following symlinks; require orchestrator ownership, exact modes, resolved-root containment, immutable source/commit/digest match, and an unrelocated configured root. Missing, altered, relocated, ownership-invalid, mode-invalid, or symlinked locator, package, or custody object fails closed with no worktree or environment fallback.

exclusive_responsibilities: issue taskplane.expanded-lens-route-action/v1 only after exact approval validation
read production time from the provider process real system clock
verify the approval receipt using exact RSA-PSS/SHA-256 parameters
atomically consume each action once before returning a provider-sealed consumption receipt

rsa_verification.message: canonical UTF-8 JSON bytes of the closed approval receipt payload
rsa_verification.key_selection: exact approved key fingerprint from the protected approver-key manifest

expanded_route_authority.issued_action_seal: HMAC-SHA-256 over canonical UTF-8 JSON of every binding field using the provider issuer key held only in 0600 external custody; verification and compare-and-swap consumption occur only inside the provider process
expanded_route_authority.atomic_consume: Under an external authority lock, compare unused state, append the consume receipt, fsync the record, atomically rename the updated head, fsync the containing directory, and only then return success; concurrent consumers can produce at most one success.

clock.production: The production provider constructor and command expose no clock parameter and read real time only inside the trusted provider process.
clock.tests: Deterministic clock injection exists only in a non-exported trusted-provider test fixture using a temporary external provider root; production construction rejects it.

closed_invariants: exactly one disposition for every catalog lens in catalog order
only execute_deep and execute_light rows appear in selected
covered_by targets one selected lens and coverage edges are acyclic
mandatory risk floors are applied before cap or deduplication
equal canonical context, catalog, and policy version produce byte-identical decision material

approval_policy.human_approval: final delivery sign-off only after EM synthesis
approval_policy.orchestrator_only: Only the root orchestrator may gate or approve Design, Plan, Build, Evaluate, Fix, or EM transitions.

proposed_edges.reason: The incumbent dependency-neutral detector supplies complete scored rows and mandatory risk-floor evidence to the pure selector.
The catalog adapter projects existing scores into the canonical context and converts selected dispositions into dispatch briefs.
The pure policy owns deterministic stage selection, count rules, risk deduplication, and overflow refusal.
The pure policy validates the exact 26-row closed disposition ledger and selected-set conservation.
Product, Design, and Plan stage adapters build fresh stage-specific contexts and mechanically gate their artifacts.
ReviewKernel builds Evaluate context from the actual diff, impact, tests, and findings before minting any slot.
Loop dispatch confines lens execution to routed decision stages and emits zero-lens Build/Fix/EM authority.
Closed native lifecycle observations prove zero Taskplane lens starts for Build, Fix, and EM without suppressing Evaluate.
The worktree adapter may serialize a closed request and consume a provider-sealed decision, but cannot issue, verify, time, locate, or consume authority.

The graph-selected durably-protected-issuer demonstrates root-private key custody, authority locking, atomic immutable writes, directory fsync, and explicit restart recovery; the new provider follows this pattern with separate keys and lifecycle.
The packaged provider exclusively validates the external content-addressed locator, 0600 keys/manifests/journals, real clock, exact RSA receipt, and atomic one-use state.
The orchestrator executes only the exact immutable packaged object in a separate trusted interpreter after source, commit, digest, location, ownership, mode, and no-symlink validation.
Only the protected provider may issue, validate authoritative time, perform exact RSA-PSS verification, atomically consume once, and seal the dispatch receipt.
ReviewKernel permits an expanded dispatch only when the provider-sealed consumption receipt binds its exact current route and context fingerprint.
ReviewKernel seals route input, route decision, per-lens input fingerprints, reused results, leases, and new results as one conserved evidence set.
Fix-to-Evaluate comparison reuses only sealed passing evidence with an equal canonical per-lens input fingerprint.
The existing immutable usage ledger gains a closed bounded stage-route record for cost, runtime, reuse, invalidation, and terminal state.
Product authority records the complete routed-stage transparency and acceptance contract.
The Design Contract fixes the stage policies, boundaries, route schema, and rollout before implementation.
Plan maps the approved stage rules and every designed edge to dependency-aware implementation and validation tasks.
Unit and mutation tests reject missing, duplicate, unsupported, cyclic, and unevidenced dispositions.

Provider tests reject binding mutation, tampering, replay, expiry, concurrent double-consume, stage/target mismatch, worktree clock/RSA/source monkeypatches, and any attempt to weaken mandatory floors.

Custody tests reject missing, altered, relocated, ownership/mode-invalid, and symlinked locators or objects, prove restart recovery, and confine deterministic clock injection to trusted provider tests.
Determinism and selective-invalidation tests mutate one, multiple, unchanged, and policy-version inputs.
Schema, bound, redaction, token, runtime, reuse, and invalidation telemetry tests prove complete privacy-safe records.
Role contracts explain which stages apply focused quick lenses and forbid Build/Fix nested lens execution.
The facade and harness route stage work without prompting users to select lenses.
Routing, catalog, state, configuration, and onboarding docs describe focused execution, overflow, reuse, and observability truthfully.
README product truth states the normal focused routes, 3–4 Plan/Evaluate bound, and separate explicit all-deep audit.

risks.risk: Stage adapters supply semantically different context for the same evidence and break determinism.
risks.mitigation: Use one closed context schema, canonical serializer, shared policy version, catalog fingerprint, cross-stage fixtures, and key-order mutation tests.

risks.risk: Risk deduplication marks two independent mandatory concerns as covered and silently narrows review.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit risk-group evidence, selected covering lens, acyclic coverage, mandatory-floor application before deduplication, and five-risk overflow mutation tests.

risks.risk: Evidence from before a Fix is reused against materially changed inputs.
risks.mitigation: Bind reuse to per-lens canonical input fingerprints, policy/catalog version, sealed passing result, and host provenance; default every uncertainty to invalidated.

risks.risk: A worker replaces provider source, clock, RSA verification, locator, issuance, or consumption and turns expanded-route authority into a generic or replayable bypass.
risks.mitigation: Execute only the exact content-addressed packaged provider in a separate orchestrator process; validate external 0600 custody without symlinks or fallback; bind source/commit/digests, workspace, stage, target, context, exact lenses/cost/policy/action/expiry/approver/receipt; use provider-owned real time, exact RSA-PSS verification, and atomic one-use consumption.

risks.risk: The protected provider or external custody is unavailable, invalid, or rolled back during overflow.
risks.mitigation: Fail closed with zero expanded dispatch and preserve normal routes; require a deterministic split or a repaired/reinstalled exact provider. Never fall back to worktree authority or alter immutable receipts/consumed state.

risks.risk: The existing zero-lens delivery authority continues to suppress Evaluate.
risks.mitigation: Separate Build/Fix/EM zero-lens validation from Evaluate routing and add positive Evaluate-dispatch plus negative Build/Fix/EM lifecycle tests.

risks.risk: Route evidence or telemetry leaks raw prompts, diffs, secrets, workstation identity, or absolute paths.
risks.mitigation: Persist bounded reason codes, repository-relative paths, pseudonymous targets, content hashes, closed schemas, and explicit privacy mutation tests.

risks.risk: Legacy route history is mistaken for current dispatch or reuse authority.
risks.mitigation: Keep a one-generation read-only renderer that cannot authorize dispatch/reuse and require focused-routing/v1 for every new gate.

failure_modes.mode: A stage context, disposition ledger, or selected set violates its closed schema.
failure_modes.recovery: The owning stage adapter emits routing_policy_unavailable, dispatches zero lens workers, and the stage owner corrects the named context or ledger before retrying the same target.

failure_modes.mode: Plan or Evaluate has more than four independent mandatory risks.
failure_modes.recovery: The planner/evaluator splits the target along the deterministic disjoint scopes, or the human supplies one exact signed expanded-route capability before dispatch.

failure_modes.mode: A Fix changes one or more canonical inputs for previously selected lens evidence.
failure_modes.recovery: ReviewKernel reuses only equal sealed pass fingerprints, mints new leases for every invalidated or newly selected lens, and refuses completion until their results collect.

failure_modes.mode: An expanded-route action is tampered, replayed, expired, or bound to another target/context.
failure_modes.recovery: The protected provider rejects it with zero dispatch and preserves its consumption journal; the orchestrator requests a new exact action only if the human still authorizes the same current route.

failure_modes.mode: The provider source, commit, digest, external locator, ownership, mode, custody, or resolved location is missing, altered, relocated, or symlinked.
failure_modes.recovery: Disable expanded dispatch. The orchestrator repairs or reinstalls the exact immutable provider/custody under the configured protected root and reruns validation; it never imports worktree source or accepts an environment fallback.

failure_modes.mode: A worker monkeypatches its clock, RSA helper, provider locator, issuance helper, or consume helper.
failure_modes.recovery: The separately executed provider remains authoritative and returns only its sealed result. Record the rejected/probed request without sensitive material; no worker-supplied callable or time value crosses the request schema.

failure_modes.mode: Two processes attempt to consume the same valid expanded-route action.
failure_modes.recovery: The provider authority lock and durable compare-and-swap permit one sealed success; all other consumers fail closed and ReviewKernel accepts only the unique consumption receipt.

failure_modes.mode: A Taskplane lens worker starts during Build, Fix, or EM.
failure_modes.recovery: The loop blocks the stage gate, terminalizes the offending child contract, preserves the native trace, and reruns only after the stage dispatch is corrected.

failure_modes.mode: Immutable route or telemetry persistence fails before the stage pointer is updated.
failure_modes.recovery: The storage owner leaves the previous pointer authoritative, removes or quarantines the incomplete temporary object, and retries the atomic write without dispatching from partial evidence.

failure_modes.mode: Estimated or actual lens usage is absent, non-finite, negative, or exceeds its schema bound.
failure_modes.recovery: The telemetry owner marks the route incomplete, blocks terminal route accounting, and reconstructs usage only from the sealed native receipt; it never guesses a value.

alerts: Block the current stage immediately when lens_route_validation_failure or route_artifact_write_failure is emitted.
Require human-visible overflow handling when lens_route_overflow is emitted and no deterministic split is available.
Block Build/Fix/EM completion on any build_fix_lens_start_violation.
Surface repeated expanded_route_authority_rejection after two attempts for the same target fingerprint without weakening validation.
Block expanded dispatch immediately on any provider source, custody, RSA, or replay rejection; do not substitute worktree code, time, verification, or state.
Alert on any expanded_route_worker_boundary_probe and on more than one expanded_route_provider_issuance for the same action id.
Fail the cost/reuse ratchet when lens_route_dispatch_count exceeds four without a valid expanded-route receipt or when unchanged evidence launches a worker.

rollout.strategy: Preserve completed LR-01, LR-02, LR-04, LR-05, and LR-03 commits/evidence; replan only LR-03 and blocked downstream work for canonical finding 6ea9aff0107f4bb6. Package expanded_route_authority_provider.py as an immutable content-addressed provider; install its external protected locator/custody; make taskplane_lite request-only; run source/custody/RSA/binding/replay/race/restart/worker-monkeypatch tests; then continue quick-only Product/Design, 3–4 quick Plan/Evaluate, zero-lens Build/Fix, clean-package smoke, strict graph verification, and final-only human sign-off.
rollout.rollback: Disable or remove only the external provider locator while retaining immutable approval, issuance, and consumption records. Normal routes of at most four lenses continue; overflow must split or fail closed. Never restore worktree-side issuance, time, RSA verification, or consumption. Before release the provider code may be reverted; after artifacts exist, preserve their readers and history without rewriting evidence.

python_runtime.execution_model: synchronous pure policy plus a synchronous protected provider command executed by the orchestrator in a separate trusted process; existing stage owners retain cancellation, interruption, handoff, and child lifecycle control
python_runtime.mutable_shared_state: none in lens_route_policy.py; expanded provider issuance and one-use state are external and serialized by an authority lock with durable atomic transitions, never by worker globals or GIL behavior
python_runtime.free_threaded: safe by construction for the pure policy; provider correctness depends on filesystem authority locking and durable compare-and-swap rather than GIL serialization; no extension modules are introduced
python_runtime.packaging: existing Taskplane plugin/package namespace includes lens_route_policy.py and expanded_route_authority_provider.py; installation copies the latter to providers/expanded-route/<source-sha256>/expanded_route_authority_provider.py with an immutable manifest binding source path, commit, source digest, package digest, and protocol version; authority executes only that verified object with no network or worktree fallback
